title: Siliguri Police Gives Sweets & 'Phool' Instead Of Challan To Riders Without Helmet: 'Mera To Rs 5,000 Ka Fine Tha' | Viral News - News18
text: The traffic police of Siliguri in West Bengal hosted a unique awareness program for two-wheelers approaching the road without helmets. Instead of coming down harshly against the offenders and imposing a penalty on them, the traffic authorities amusingly passed on their message. They handed over roses and sweets to those who had mistakenly taken the routes without wearing helmets. The idea was to encourage people to follow the traffic regulations themselves without being forced to do so in the fear of punishment. A video perfectly captured the Siliguri traffic police’s awareness program, as they stopped multiple people operating on two-wheelers and gave them roses and sweets before quietly asking them to wear a helmet next time. Siliguri Police’s Sweet Awareness Program The video starts with a woman bursting into laughter, feeling a touch embarrassed, as one of the traffic police officers handed her a flower before the other one gave her sweets to eat while she sat on her scooty without wearing a helmet. One of the other officers also recorded the moment. All three officers were themselves wearing the helmet to put the point across. The traffic officers caught multiple other people, including a young man driving a bike with another youngster and a woman sitting in the back. In a two-fold offence, he was neither wearing a helmet nor following the restriction against three-person sitting. But the traffic police showed remarkable patience with him as well and stuck to their task, handing him a flower and sweets to eat. ‘Me Purposely Going For Ladoo’ As the video of the Siliguri traffic police’s awareness program and unique tactic to press home their point gained traction, the online community naturally switched its creative brains on and came up with an array of remarks. One person wondered if they could deliberately reach the site for the flower and the sweets. “Me purposely going without a helmet in front of them just for ladoo," quipped an individual. “Happy to see this, no gender bias," laughed another person after the traffic police also caught the female offender. Someone else asked, “Siliguri police romantic kab se ho gaya (when did Siliguri police get romantic?)." It was indeed an exceptional idea to encourage people to follow the traffic guidelines by the Siliguri traffic police. The authorities wanted to inculcate good road ethics in two-wheeler owners instead of forcing them to abide by the regulations out of fear of punishment.
